question: Will Germany beat Serbia in their UEFA Nations League match on 13 November 2026?

calls.reasoning: Base rate for a top European side away to a much weaker European side in competitive matches is ~55-65% win. Germany is far stronger on paper and beat Serbia 2-0 on 1 Oct; Serbia has lost 6 straight (incl. 1-5 Mexico, 0-3 Cape Verde) and the match is behind closed doors (UEFA sanction), cutting home advantage. Against: Germany's form under Klopp is mediocre (1W 2D 1L in group, 3 goals in 4; earlier loss to Ecuador, draw with Paraguay) and they may rotate before the Netherlands game. Market: search snippet shows FanDuel Germany -475 (~80% vig-free) but couldn't verify (403), and that looks rich for an away game; Kickoff.co.uk model 79% may be for the earlier home match. No Polymarket/Kalshi/Manifold match market; the Polymarket candidates are outright/relegation contracts, not matches. Partial lean toward the market from my ~60% prior.

calls.reconciliation: Disputes: (1) the closed-doors sanction is factual. Runs 1 and 3 cite independent reports (Sportschau, bluewin, Yahoo) and Run 2 does not contradict them, so I accept it, which lowers home advantage. (2) FanDuel -475 is factual and unverifiable: all runs saw a 403, and it is implausibly shorter than the 1.33 home price, so I discount it. (3) Reference-class level and rotation weight are judgment. Converting the home price of about 75% with the home/away swing, damped by the closed doors, gives about 60-62%. I take 0.61.
